comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: vendored QuickJS engine is 3 upstream releases behind — document a security re-vendor path**

This bump makes the vendored QuickJS **2024-01-13** C engine the preferred JS backend on all VM platforms (`js_widget_runtime` 0.4.180's default backend selects `QuickjsFfi.isAvailable ? QuickjsWidgetEngineBackend : FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend` — the Native Asset now builds on iOS/Android/macOS/Linux thanks to the fork), i.e. user-supplied app scripts now execute in an app-bundled engine instead of the OS-patched JavaScriptCore that the flutter_js backend used on iOS.

The vendored sources are pinned at 2024-01-13 (`hook/build.dart` `CONFIG_VERSION: '"2024-01-13"'`; `native/quickjs/*.c` headers copyright 2017-2021), but upstream QuickJS has published **2025-04-26, 2025-09-13 and 2026-06-04** since (https://bellard.org/quickjs/, read during this review) — three releases of engine fixes the vendored copy will never receive on its own.

The fork's own lifecycle note (`vendor/quickjs_runtime/CHANGELOG.md` "Re-vendor … on the next upstream publish that fixes **both**") only triggers on the next `quickjs_runtime` publish that fixes the Android/Windows **build** breaks — there is no documented trigger or path for pulling **engine** security fixes into this fork.

Please add a short security note to `vendor/quickjs_runtime/CHANGELOG.md` (or the fork header in `hook/build.dart`): which party tracks QuickJS upstream releases/security advisories for this vendored engine, and what the re-vendor/upgrade path is (e.g. "re-vendor from the next quickjs_runtime that tracks quickjs ≥ 2026-06-04" or an explicit risk acceptance with an owner). The engineering in this PR is clean — this is only about making the upgrade trigger explicit before the fork ages in place.

(Non-blocking: behavior is the ticket's stated intent — #1784 needs the synchronous FFI lane — and CI is green.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: PR description doesn't mention ~½ of the final diff**

The PR body covers the jsr bump, the store/codesign hardening, size budgets and the gh-1784 gesture wiring — but two substantial parts of the shipped diff are invisible to a description-only reader:

1. **The vendored fork** (`vendor/quickjs_runtime/` — 49 upstream files + the Android/Windows hook deltas + the 3 CodeQL-driven C casts) and the `dependency_overrides` pin consumed here — the whole reason this override exists.
2. **The wrap-perf gate hardening** (`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — best-of-3 attempt medians for the absolute budgets), which fixed the validation red that blocked this PR's own CI.

Both are well documented in the review-thread rework comments, but the description is the durable record. Please append a short "Rework additions" section listing them (and the pin test that guards the override) so future readers don't have to reconstruct the scope from the discussion history.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `tool/build_quickjs.sh` still links `-lpthread` unconditionally — the exact break this PR fixes in the hook**

The Native-Assets hook now excludes `pthread` on Android (bionic ships pthread in libc; the NDK has no `libpthread` since r18 — `ld.lld: error: unable to find library -lpthread`), but this manual build script kept the unconditional `-lm ... -lpthread`, so anyone building the bridge by hand against the NDK reproduces the CI error this PR just fixed. The script already pattern-matches `uname -s` for the Windows `-ldl` case; the same `case` could drop `pthread` for Android environments (e.g. when `CC` names an `*android*` cross-compiler or `$ANDROID_NDK` is set), keeping script and hook consistent.

Related nit: the script's output (`native/quickjs/libquickjs_bridge.so`, ~940 KB) is not covered by `.gitignore`'s vendor-artifact rules (`vendor/**/target|build|.dart_tool`), so a local manual build leaves an untracked binary in `git status`. One line — `vendor/quickjs_runtime/native/quickjs/libquickjs_bridge.so` — closes it (the Native Assets build output under `build/` is already ignored).

Dev-only path, not blocking.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: typo in the quoted CI error — `ld.ld:` → `ld.lld:`**

The header comment quoting the Android link failure reads `ld.ld: error: unable to find library -lpthread`; the linker is `ld.lld`. The same quote is spelled correctly on line 127 of this very file (the test reason string), in `hook/build.dart` and in the vendor `CHANGELOG.md` — worth aligning so a future grep for the real CI error text also finds this header.

comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: Solid, verified fork: vendored `quickjs_runtime` is byte-identical to upstream pub.dev 0.4.2 (sha256 match; recursive diff = only the 4 documented deltas), the 3 C widening casts are value-identical under their existing guards, and the `onGestureEvent` wiring matches the renderer contract in all three surfaces. One important security-posture doc gap (vendored QuickJS 2024-01-13 is now the preferred JS engine on all VM platforms but is 3 upstream releases behind, with no documented engine re-vendor trigger) and 3 suggestions; nothing blocking.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT — no documented security re-vendor path for the vendored engine (`vendor/quickjs_runtime/CHANGELOG.md`; upstream published 2025-04-26 / 2025-09-13 / 2026-06-04 since 2024-01-13)
- 💡 SUGGESTION — PR description omits the vendored fork and the wrap-perf hardening (half the final diff)
- 💡 SUGGESTION — `tool/build_quickjs.sh` still links `-lpthread` (Android) and its `.so` output isn't gitignored
- 💡 SUGGESTION — `ld.ld:` → `ld.lld:` typo in the pin-test header

**Verified this run**: provenance (sha256 + full byte-diff vs pristine upstream 0.4.2), fork-delta value-preservation arguments at all 3 C sites, pin/guard suites 17/17, wrap-perf 14/14, flutter app tests 35 pass / 6 skip (incl. the new gh-1784 gesture tests), `dart analyze` clean, size-budget arithmetic (+950,272 both TSVs) correct, vendor tree excluded from repo gates/publish payload per the established `vendor/dart_tui`/`wasm_run` pattern.

**Next Steps**:
1. Document the engine security re-vendor path in `vendor/quickjs_runtime/CHANGELOG.md`
2. Align `tool/build_quickjs.sh` with the hook's Android library set + add the `.so` gitignore rule
3. Update the PR description with a "Rework additions" section (fork + wrap-perf hardening)
4. Fix the `ld.lld` typo in the pin-test header
